title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Water
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: FBI and EPA: coordinated attacks have hit water utilities in at least seven states; Minnesota hardest
items.content_text: On 30–31 July the FBI and EPA issued a public-service alert — and CISA a companion warning of a “significant escalation” — confirming that malicious actors have struck internet-facing OT at water and wastewater utilities in at least seven states since 27 July, degrading operations. The attackers reached exposed Rockwell Allen-Bradley MicroLogix 1100 and 1400 controllers, changed their IP addresses and passwords, and left operators without remote monitoring or control. Minnesota was hit hardest — more than 30 systems, with Braham’s plant briefly offline, boil-water notices issued and several communities running on manual control. Researchers assess Iran-linked CyberAv3ngers as the likely actor, possibly abusing the unpatched Rockwell flaw CVE-2021-22681, but the government has not formally attributed it. No utility has reported contaminated drinking water.

_otthreatfeed.source_name: FBI/EPA PSA & CISA alert / NBC News, Cybersecurity Dive — FBI confirmed
_otthreatfeed.date_note: Attacks since 27 Jul 2026 — FBI/EPA/CISA alerts 30–31 Jul

items.title: Iran-affiliated actors are manipulating water-system PLC logic (AA26-097A, updated 22 Jul)
items.content_text: The mechanism behind the Minnesota disruption is spelled out in advisory AA26-097A, updated 22 July. Federal agencies confirm Iran-affiliated actors are reaching internet-exposed PLCs — Unitronics, Rockwell and, newly, Schneider Modicon and Siemens S7-1200 — using the same engineering software legitimate operators use, extracting project files, and rewriting or deleting control logic. In some cases they disabled shutdown and alarm functions so equipment can drift into unsafe states without alerting staff. The update documents project-file exfiltration for the first time and adds detection guidance for tampering with reusable code modules. For a small utility the exposed devices are ordinary dosing, pump and lift-station controllers left reachable with default or shared passwords.

items.title: FSB Center 16 router campaign (AA26-194A): exposed edge gear in front of municipal water SCADA
items.content_text: A joint advisory from NSA, CISA, the FBI and ~12 partner nations (AA26-194A, 13 July) details how Russia’s FSB Center 16 — Static Tundra / Berserk Bear / Energetic Bear / Dragonfly — scans for devices exposing SNMP with default community strings and abuses Cisco Smart Install to copy device configs. State and local government is named explicitly, which is what most municipal water utilities are. The same internet-facing edge routers sit in front of treatment-plant and lift-station SCADA, and a stolen config is a ready-made map before an intruder touches a controller.

items.title: Researchers tie the water attacks to CyberAv3ngers and an unpatchable Rockwell flaw
items.content_text: Analysis from Tenable, Dragos and others points at Iran’s IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers as the likely hand behind the Minnesota and multi-state disruptions, though the government has not formally attributed them. The suspected route is CVE-2021-22681, a critical (CVSS 9.8) authentication-bypass in Rockwell Logix controllers with no vendor patch — it was added to CISA’s KEV in March 2026 after confirmed Iranian-affiliated exploitation. The same crew earlier hijacked 75+ Unitronics Vision PLCs at water utilities using the default ‘1111’ password. The pattern is consistent: internet-exposed, weakly-authenticated controllers, chosen for public visibility rather than a single vendor bug. Treat any exposed Rockwell, Unitronics, Schneider or Siemens controller as in-scope regardless of utility size.

items.title: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day (CVSS 10) exploited — added to CISA KEV
items.content_text: CISA added Arista’s VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw CVE-2026-16812 (CVSS 10.0) to the KEV catalog on 27 July after it was exploited as a zero-day. It is an unauthenticated OS command-injection bug in on-prem VCO — the console that manages VeloCloud SD-WAN edges — needing only network reach to the web interface, with a 30 July federal fix deadline. Multi-site water utilities increasingly use SD-WAN to link plants, tanks and lift stations, so a compromised orchestrator is a direct path toward the OT network. CISA added a second flaw the same day, Fortinet FortiOS CVE-2025-68686 (CVSS 5.3, information exposure), which requires prior file-system access.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Added to KEV 27 Jul 2026 — actively exploited

items.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center zero-day exploited — hard-coded password on the IT/OT boundary
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-20316 to the KEV catalog on 29 July after Cisco confirmed active exploitation before a patch existed. The flaw is a hard-coded password in Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (formerly Firepower Management Center) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker log in with a low-privilege account and read sensitive data — firewall rules, VPN configs, device inventory and event logs. That console often governs the firewalls separating a utility’s IT from its plant OT, so even limited access is valuable reconnaissance for lateral movement toward SCADA. Any water utility running FMC should patch and pull its management interface off the internet.

_otthreatfeed.date_note: Added to KEV 29 Jul 2026 — actively exploited

items.title: EPA’s 2026 National Cyber Drill tests whether water still flows when the network doesn’t
items.content_text: The EPA launched its 2026 National Cybersecurity Drill challenging drinking-water and wastewater utilities to keep critical functions running when telecom and internet access are degraded or gone. The scenario forces operations in a “disconnected” state — limited or no SCADA remote connectivity, cloud services, email or VoIP — to test manual fallback and sector resilience. Participation is a low-cost way to pressure-test whether a utility can run blind.

items.title: Congress temporarily extends water cyber authorities as EPA issues new guidance
items.content_text: Congress temporarily extended lapsing water-sector cybersecurity legal authorities while the EPA released new guidance for utilities, keeping the federal support structure in place amid ongoing debate over a permanent regulatory model for water. For utilities the practical signal is continuity: baseline expectations and available federal resources remain, and permanent requirements may still be coming.
